payload.analysis: Combined with suspected nasopharyngeal lesion headache, MRI shows bilateral nasopharyngeal lesions with restricted diffusion, endoscopy reveals enlarged cystic torus tubarius with purulent drainage, and biopsy confirms benign reactive lymphoid hyperplasia with mild chronic inflammation. These findings support an organic inflammatory nasopharyngeal source capable of causing refractory headache, while weakening PTSD/TBI and primary tension-type headache explanations. Contrast-enhanced MRI and audiometry remain missing, but all currently retrievable key imaging and pathologic information is covered.

focus.label: The nasopharyngeal lesions are benign reactive inflammatory lesions
focus.why: MRI shows restricted diffusion in bilateral torus tubarii lesions, biopsy demonstrates benign respiratory mucosa with reactive lymphoid hyperplasia and mild chronic inflammation, and endoscopy reveals purulent drainage from an enlarged cystic torus tubarius. Expert analyses uniformly interpret these findings as inflammatory/reactive rather than malignant, supporting a benign reactive inflammatory process with high confidence.
